newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech Komercni lowers reference rate to 12.25 pct. [CORRECTED 15:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Czech Komercni lowers reference rate to 12.25 pct. [CORRECTED 15:00 GMT]

text.p: The largest Czech commerical bank, Komercni Banka a.s., said on Wednesday it would lower its key interest rate on credit, the reference rate, 10 basis points to 12.25 percent from January 30.
Komercni said in a statement the rate, used to align the bank's entire credit offering to clients, was lowered to reflect movement of interest rates on the interbank deposit market.
On January 22, Komercni changed its reference rate for the first time this year to 12.35 percent from 12.6 percent, citing the same reasons.

On Wednesday, the Prague Interbank Offer Rate (PRIBOR) for six-month money, which Komercni uses as a guage for setting its reference rate, dipped 10 basis points to 11.58 percent from 11.68 percent on Tuesday.
The Czech National Bank's discount rate has remained at 10.5 percent since it was raised (corrects from lowered) one percentage point last June.

Komercni also said it would lower the fixed rate 40 basis points on time deposits for maturities up to one year, 30 basis points on maturities from one to two years and 10 basis points for deposits for three to five years.
It said the revisions to the deposit rates corresponded to the easing of credit rates on the money and capital markets.
